title: HarperCollins Is Launching Kazé in the U.S., and Manga Publishing Just Got a New Heavyweight
description: HarperCollins is launching Kazé as a dedicated U.S. manga imprint, with seven licenses due to be revealed later in 2026.

hero.alt: AniManga Updates with Old Man Otaku

research_notes: ICv2 reports HarperCollins is launching Kazé as a U.S. manga imprint and plans to reveal seven initial licenses later in 2026.
The imprint is reported to span children's through adult readership.
Do not frame this as HarperCollins entering manga for the first time. HarperCollins already has U.S. manga activity, including HarperAlley manga and adult graphic novels.
HarperCollins acquired Crunchyroll's manga publishing businesses in France and Germany in 2025. Those operations became Pegasus Manga companies.
The historic KAZÉ brand returned for new European releases beginning in April 2026.
HarperCollins previously described the revived KAZÉ strategy as international and multinational in ambition.

scenes.headline: A New Manga Heavyweight?
scenes.body: HarperCollins is launching Kazé as a dedicated U.S. manga imprint.

scenes.headline: Seven Licenses Incoming
scenes.body: The first seven titles are expected to be revealed later in 2026, covering readers from kids through adults.

scenes.headline: Kazé Isn't Actually New
scenes.body: The brand has decades of European manga history and was revived by HarperCollins after its 2025 Crunchyroll publishing acquisition.

scenes.headline: This Is Bigger Than 7 Books
scenes.body: HarperCollins brings global trade distribution, production infrastructure and retailer relationships to a dedicated manga line.

scenes.headline: The Real Question
scenes.body: Will Kazé chase blockbuster licenses, underserved manga, children's titles, or all of the above? The first seven books will tell us.

scenes.headline: Manga Has Another Player
scenes.body: This isn't HarperCollins discovering manga. It's HarperCollins formalizing a much bigger U.S. manga strategy. Full story at RogueVerseMedia.com.
